minutes.headline: Assessors voted to accept the consultant's waterfront land-value report; abatement hearings will use its recommendations.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors recessed to read the just-received final report from Municipal Financial Services on waterfront land valuation, then took public questions about its effect on abatements, public access to the data, and filing deadlines. The board voted to accept the report, then entered executive session without returning to open session. Board members said they would likely handle each abatement individually using the consultant's recommendations as a foundation.

public_comment.topic: Point of order on whether public comment would follow the recess and whether discussion could occur during the recess; told comment follows.
Asked whether the report packet contains private information and whether spreadsheet data from the consultant can be shared publicly with private columns removed, and the turnaround.
Asked what effect the final report will have on the abatement process, when the board will meet on abatements, and what happens to waterfront properties that did not apply for abatements.
Asked when the report will be available at the office/online, and warned that people claiming to be assessors have been going onto properties without notice.
Asked when the board will resume in-person meetings; raised concern that residents who did not file abatements before the deadline will face higher bills.
Asked whether the board will do individual abatements or an across-the-board change once it has the consultant's numbers.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted to accept the final report from Municipal Financial Services on Lunenburg waterfront property values, dated May 2023.
The board recessed to read the report, which it had received that day, before taking public questions.
Board members said they will probably take each abatement individually, using the consultant's recommendations as the foundation.
The report will be posted on the assessors' web page, with copies at the assessors' office.
The board went into executive session after the vote and did not return to open session.

why_it_matters: Waterfront owners' abatement outcomes will be set by the consultant's land-value recommendations, and a resident who did not file by the deadline may face a different bill than one who did, which residents raised and the board did not answer in this meeting.
The accepted report is the document a waterfront owner would need to read before an abatement hearing; the minutes record questions about sharing its underlying data but no decision on it.
watch_next: The posting of the MFS report on the assessors' web page and at the assessors' office.
A later vote on the format of abatement hearings, which the chair said would be taken after he proposed brief public comment followed by executive session.
